Confusable pairs among tire checks, mirror and seat settings, belt fit, child restraint stages, load securing and assistance features, followed by continuation facts; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec05-R01 | anchor: A02
When the gauge shows more pressure than the doorframe number you release air, and when it shows less you add air until the two readings agree. [A02]
Why it matters: group tires; confusable reading above versus below the doorframe number.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-R02 | anchor: A02
The gauge check measures tire pressure in PSI, while the penny check measures tread depth, so they are two different inspections. [A02]
Why it matters: group tires; confusable pressure versus tread.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-R03 | anchor: A04
The rearview mirror is set to frame the whole rear window, and a day/night mirror must be switched to suit the time of day you are driving. [A04]
Why it matters: group mirrors; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-R04 | anchor: A05
The right outside mirror uses a different method from the left: lean right until your head is under the rearview mirror or over the center console, then adjust until the right edge of your vehicle is just visible. [A05]
Why it matters: group mirrors; confusable left versus right mirror method.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-R05 | anchor: A03
The steering wheel limit is about height, with its top no higher than your shoulders, while the head restraint limit is about contact, touching the back of your head and not sitting below your ears. [A03]
Why it matters: group seating; confusable wheel height versus head restraint height.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-R06 | anchor: A06
The shoulder part of the belt goes across the shoulder and chest, while the lap part goes snug and low across the hips, and each misplaced part brings its own collision injury risk. [A06]
Why it matters: group belts; confusable shoulder harness versus lap belt.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-R07 | anchor: A07
The back seat rule covers children age seven and younger in a car seat, while the adult belt rule starts at age 8 or a height of 57 inches, so the two rules answer different questions. [A07]
Why it matters: group child passengers; confusable seating position versus restraint type.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-R08 | anchor: A07
Moving a child from a rear-facing to a forward-facing seat depends on age two or on outgrowing the rear-facing seat's height or weight limit, not on age alone. [A07]
Why it matters: group child passengers; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-R09 | anchor: A08
A booster seat is held in place by both the lap and the shoulder belt, not by the lap belt alone. [A08]
Why it matters: group child passengers; confusable lap only versus lap and shoulder.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec05-R10 | anchor: A08
Do not overload your vehicle or trailer, double-check every load before leaving, and remember that animals you carry must also be properly secured. [A08]
Why it matters: group loads; difficulty low.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec05-R11 | anchor: A09
Before driving with a load, ask whether anything could fall or blow off, whether it is secured at the back, sides and top, how it would react to hard braking, a bump or a crash, and whether you would feel safe driving behind it. [A09]
Why it matters: group loads; difficulty low.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec05-R12 | anchor: A09
Some assistance features only warn you with sounds or vibration, while others can step in by adjusting the braking or steering. [A09]
Why it matters: group assistance features; confusable alert versus intervention.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec05-R13 | anchor: A09
Cruise control and parking assist are both named as features you may not use during the driving test, even though parking assist is listed among the safety features. [A09]
Why it matters: group assistance features; difficulty medium.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec05-R14 | anchor: A10
Keep vehicle sensors clean and free of damage, and keep the software up to date where it applies, following the vehicle maker's recommendations. [A10]
Why it matters: group assistance features; difficulty low.
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec05-R15 | anchor: A10
Used properly, assistance features offer real benefits and could help reduce crashes, injuries and deaths. [A10]
Why it matters: group assistance features; difficulty low.
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0052]
